title: Grade Calculator - Weighted Grades & Final Exam Target
description: Calculate current weighted course grades across assignments and determine the exact score needed on your final exam to hit your target grade.
quickAnswer: To calculate your weighted grade, multiply each assignment score by its syllabus weight percentage, sum the weighted scores, and divide by the total weight completed: Weighted Grade = Σ(Score × Weight) ÷ Σ(Weight). To find the score needed on a final exam, use: Required Final = (Target Grade − Current Grade Points) ÷ Final Weight. All calculations run client-side.

formula.title: Weighted Grade Formula
formula.explanation: Multiply each score by its syllabus percentage weight, sum the points, and divide by the total completed weight. To find the grade needed on the final exam: Required Final = [Target Grade × 100 − Current Weighted Points] ÷ Final Weight.

commonMistakes.title: Simple Averaging Instead of Weighting
commonMistakes.description: Taking a simple mathematical average of test scores ignores that a 20-minute quiz and a comprehensive midterm exam carry vastly different weight percentages in your syllabus.

commonMistakes.title: Failing to Normalize Incomplete Semesters
commonMistakes.description: If only 50% of coursework is completed, having 42 total accumulated points does not mean you have a 42% (F). You must divide by 0.50, revealing an 84% (B).

commonMistakes.title: Assuming 100% Weight Sum Before Finals
commonMistakes.description: Your completed assignments will rarely sum to 100% until the final exam is graded. Always account for remaining final exam weight when calculating current standing.

faqs.q: How is a weighted grade calculated?
faqs.a: To calculate a weighted grade, multiply each assignment score by its percentage weight, add all the resulting points together, and divide by the total completed weight percentage. Mathematically: Weighted Grade = Σ(Score × Weight) ÷ Σ(Weight).

faqs.q: How do you calculate what score you need on the final exam?
faqs.a: Subtract your current weighted points contribution from your total required points, then divide by the final exam's weight percentage: Required Score = (Target Points - Current Points) ÷ Final Weight. For example, if you need 30 points and the final is worth 30% of the class, you need 30 ÷ 0.30 = 100% on the final.

faqs.q: What happens if total assignment weights do not add up to 100%?
faqs.a: Our calculator automatically divides your accumulated points by the sum of completed weights. This normalizes your score to accurately represent your true current standing at any point in the semester.

faqs.q: What should I do if my syllabus uses total points instead of percentages?
faqs.a: If your syllabus uses points (e.g. Homework 200 pts, Midterm 300 pts, Final 500 pts out of 1000), divide each category's points by the total course points to find the percentage weight: 200 ÷ 1000 = 20% weight.

faqs.q: What does it mean if the calculator says I need over 100% on the final?
faqs.a: If the required score exceeds 100%, it means mathematical perfection on the final exam alone will fall short of your target grade. You would need extra credit points or a curved grading scale to reach that target.

faqs.q: What does it mean if the calculator says I need 0% or negative on the final?
faqs.a: This means you have already accumulated enough weighted points throughout the term that you are mathematically guaranteed to achieve your target grade, even with a zero on the final test.

faqs.q: Does this grade calculator save my private coursework grades?
faqs.a: No. All grade arithmetic runs purely client-side in your local browser window. No assignment names, test scores, or personal academic records are transmitted or saved.
